name: Carbohydrate and Lipid Chemistry: Stereoisomers, Glycosidic Bonds and Lipids

reference.source: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry / Medical Biochemistry 5th ed
clinicalPearls: D- and L-isomers are designated by the asymmetric carbon farthest from the carbonyl; human enzymes metabolize D-sugars
Glucose and galactose are C-4 epimers; glucose and mannose are C-2 epimers
Sucrose contains an alpha-1,beta-2 bond joining both anomeric carbons, rendering it non-reducing
Unsaturated cis-double bonds create rigid kinks that lower lipid melting point and maintain membrane fluidity
Triacylglycerols yield 37 kJ/g upon complete oxidation, providing over twice the caloric density of hydrated glycogen
reference.pathophysiology: Stereochemical configuration determines enzyme-substrate recognition and membrane architecture. Monosaccharide epimerization enables interconversion between dietary hexoses. Unsaturated fatty acid incorporation into phospholipids preserves homeoviscous adaptation in biological membranes. Adipose triacylglycerols provide high-density anhydrous energy reserves mobilized during fasting.
additionalDifferentials: Essential fructosuria (fructokinase deficiency, benign reducing sugar in urine)
Classical galactosemia (GALT deficiency, toxic galactose-1-phosphate accumulation)
additionalInvestigations: Fasting lipid profile (total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL, calculated LDL)
Urine reducing substances test (Benedict reaction) to screen for galactosuria or fructosuria
Gas chromatography of plasma fatty acid methyl esters
